During `POST /v1/settlements` and `POST /v1/settlements/{id}/entries`, `clearledger-api` maps PostgreSQL constraint and trigger exceptions (`SQLSTATE 23514`, `23503`, `23502`, `23505`, and `P0001`) to HTTP `400 Bad Request` (`invalid_settlement`).\n\n## 2. Projector Worker (`projector_image` on AWS Lambda)\n\n- **Bootstrap**: `/var/runtime/bootstrap`\n- **Trigger**: SQS event source mapping from the main SQS queue (`batch_size = 5`, `maximum_batching_window_in_seconds = 0`, `function_response_types = [\"ReportBatchItemFailures\"]`)\n- **Required environment variables**:\n  - `AWS_REGION`: region from `config.json`\n  - `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`: region from `config.json`\n  - `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`: `\"test\"`\n  - `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`: `\"test\"`\n  - `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`: `\"http://aws:4566\"`\n  - `PROJECTION_TABLE`: name of the DynamoDB projection table\n  - `VALKEY_URL`: `redis://<valkey_host>:<valkey_port>`\n  - `CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP`: name of the projector CloudWatch Log Group\n\nFor each valid event envelope in the SQS batch:\n- Inserts the event item (`PK = \"SETTLEMENT#<settlement_id>\"`, `SK = \"EVENT#<8-digit-zero-padded-version>\"`) in DynamoDB using a conditional `attribute_not_exists(PK) AND attribute_not_exists(SK)` write.\n- Updates the aggregate state item (`PK = \"SETTLEMENT#<settlement_id>\"`, `SK = \"STATE\"`, `GSI1PK = \"ACCOUNT#<account_id>\"`, `GSI1SK = \"SETTLEMENT#<settlement_id>\"`) using a conditional write only when `aggregateVersion` is strictly greater than the stored `version`. Duplicate or older versions are ignored idempotently; if an older version (such as `v1`) arrives after a newer version, any missing static metadata (`reference`, `debit_party`, `credit_party`) is backfilled without regressing `version`, `status`, or `clearing_stage`.\n- Deletes the Valkey key `clearledger:settlement:<settlement_id>`.\n- If any record fails validation or deserialization, its `messageId` is returned in `batchItemFailures` so SQS retries only the failed message and routes poison messages to the DLQ after `maxReceiveCount = 4` receives.\n\n## 3. Outbox Relay Worker (`relay_image` on AWS Lambda)\n\n- **Bootstrap**: `/var/runtime/bootstrap`\n- **Trigger**: EventBridge Scheduler every 1 minute (`rate(1 minute)`)\n- **Required environment variables**:\n  - `AWS_REGION`: region from `config.json`\n  - `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`: region from `config.json`\n  - `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`: `\"test\"`\n  - `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`: `\"test\"`\n  - `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`: `\"http://aws:4566\"`\n  - `DATABASE_URL`: `postgres://<db_username>:<db_password>@<rds_host>:<rds_port>/<db_name>`\n  - `SQS_QUEUE_URL`: URL of the main SQS event queue\n  - `OUTBOX_BATCH_SIZE`: `\"50\"` (must be explicitly set to `\"50\"`)\n  - `CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP`: name of the relay CloudWatch Log Group\n\nQueries up to `OUTBOX_BATCH_SIZE` rows from `clearledger.outbox` where `published_at IS NULL` ordered by `seq ASC`, sends each event envelope to `SQS_QUEUE_URL`, and updates `published_at = NOW(), attempts = attempts + 1, last_error = NULL`.\n\n## 4. Audit Archiver Worker (`archiver_image` on AWS Lambda)\n\n- **Bootstrap**: `/var/runtime/bootstrap`\n- **Trigger**: EventBridge Scheduler every 5 minutes (`rate(5 minutes)`)\n- **Required environment variables**:\n  - `AWS_REGION`: region from `config.json`\n  - `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`: region from `config.json`\n  - `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`: `\"test\"`\n  - `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`: `\"test\"`\n  - `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`: `\"http://aws:4566\"`\n  - `DATABASE_URL`: `postgres://<db_username>:<db_password>@<rds_host>:<rds_port>/<db_name>`\n  - `AUDIT_BUCKET`: name of the S3 audit archive bucket\n  - `AUDIT_PREFIX`: `\"ledger-audit/\"` (must be explicitly set to `\"ledger-audit/\"`)\n  - `AUDIT_BATCH_SIZE` (optional): defaults to `100`\n  - `CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP`: name of the archiver CloudWatch Log Group\n\nSelects published outbox rows (`published_at IS NOT NULL AND archived_at IS NULL`) ordered by `seq ASC`, writes a newline-delimited JSON object to `s3://<AUDIT_BUCKET>/ledger-audit/batch-<first_seq:08d>-<last_seq:08d>-<16_char_sha256_hex>.ndjson`, and sets `archived_at = NOW()`.\n\n## 5. OAuth2 Scopes and Authorization\n\nAll protected endpoints validate Bearer JWTs issued by the Cognito User Pool against `AUTH_ISSUER`, `AUTH_JWKS_URL`, and `AUTH_AUDIENCES`. Scopes are strictly non-hierarchical:\n\n- `clearledger/read`: permitted only on `GET /v1/settlements/{id}` and `GET /v1/settlements/{id}/ledger`.\n- `clearledger/write`: permitted only on `POST /v1/settlements` and `POST /v1/settlements/{id}/entries`.\n- `clearledger/admin`: permitted only on `POST /v1/admin/projections/{id}/rebuild`.\n\nMissing or invalid tokens return `401 Unauthorized`; valid tokens lacking the exact endpoint scope return `403 Forbidden`.\n\n## 6. Recovery Drills, Bidirectional Data-Plane Reconciliation, and Lifecycle\n\n- **Backlog & DLQ**: When the projector event source mapping is disabled, API writes commit to PostgreSQL and enqueue on SQS while `GET /v1/settlements/{id}` returns `404` until re-enabled. Duplicate, out-of-order, and concurrent event deliveries are handled without version regression; invalid envelopes are retried and routed to the DLQ after `maxReceiveCount = 4`.\n- **Bidirectional Multi-Store & Control-Plane Convergence in `deploy.sh`**:\n  - PostgreSQL (`clearledger.settlements`, `clearledger.events`, `clearledger.outbox`) is the authoritative system of record; DynamoDB, Valkey, and S3 are derived read/archive stores.\n  - Because `clearledger-projector` writes `EVENT#*` items conditionally with `attribute_not_exists(PK) AND attribute_not_exists(SK)` and updates `STATE` conditionally only when `aggregateVersion > current_version`, and because `clearledger-audit-archiver` only archives rows where `published_at IS NOT NULL AND archived_at IS NULL`, `deploy.sh` must converge both the control plane (security groups, IAM role policies, SQS/DLQ attributes, EventBridge schedules, CloudWatch Log Groups, Lambda environment variables, and PostgreSQL schema/constraints/triggers/indexes) and all derived data stores (SQS outbox relay, DynamoDB projections, Valkey cache entries, and the versioned S3 `ledger-audit/` archive) against PostgreSQL as specified in `services/rds.md`, `services/dynamodb.md`, `services/elasticache-valkey.md`, `services/s3.md`, `services/iam.md`, and `services/vpc.md` before exiting `0`.\n- **Prefix-Scoped Teardown in `destroy.sh`**:\n  - `destroy.sh` must cleanly tear down all Terraform-managed resources as well as any out-of-band operational resources or policy attachments/versions scoped to `<resource_prefix>` (by name prefix or `ClearLedgerDeployment = <resource_prefix>` tag, including customer-managed KMS keys scheduled for deletion) while keeping all `cl-base-*` baseline resources intact.\n- **Structured Logs**: All four workloads emit JSON log lines containing `correlationId` (propagated from `X-Correlation-Id`) to their configured CloudWatch Log Groups without leaking `db_password` or Cognito `client_secret` values.\n\n\n# ClearLedger Infrastructure Contract\n\nProvision the ClearLedger clearing and settlement platform using Terraform or OpenTofu in `/workspace/submission/infra` with local state stored at `/workspace/submission/infra/terraform.tfstate`.\n\n## Required Input Source\n\nRead runtime inputs from `/workspace/config/config.json`:\n\n- `resource_prefix`: unique prefix for this deployment (for example `cl-a1b2c3`)\n- `region`: AWS region (`us-east-1`)\n- `aws_endpoint_url`: AWS control-plane endpoint (`http://aws:4566`)\n- `db_name`, `db_username`, `db_password`: PostgreSQL database name and credentials\n- `api_image`, `projector_image`, `relay_image`, `archiver_image`: container image references\n- `api_image_id`, `projector_image_id`, `relay_image_id`, `archiver_image_id`: image digest identifiers\n\nEvery taggable AWS resource created by your configuration must carry the tag `ClearLedgerDeployment = <resource_prefix>` (at least 25 tagged resources) and have its name or identifier prefixed with `<resource_prefix>`. No role may grant `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on any of the other KMS keys, `ecs_execution_role_arn` and `scheduler_role_arn` must not grant access to any of the four KMS keys, and every role must explicitly deny (`Effect = \"Deny\"`) `kms:DisableKey` and `kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion` on all four customer-managed KMS keys (`database`, `messaging`, `projection`, `audit`).\n- **Defense-in-depth explicit `Deny` guardrail statements**: Do not rely solely on implicit omission for forbidden permissions. Every role's policy document must include explicit `Effect = \"Deny\"` statement(s) covering `kms:DisableKey` and `kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion` on all four KMS keys as well as all forbidden actions and resources listed under **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)** for that role below.\n- **Out-of-band IAM policy drift reconciliation in `deploy.sh`**: During `deploy.sh`, any out-of-band inline policies or attached managed policies added to any of the six ClearLedger IAM roles outside Terraform/OpenTofu must be removed so that each role retains only its canonical least-privilege policy, and any unattached customer-managed IAM policies prefixed with `<resource_prefix>` must also be deleted.\n\n## Role Responsibilities and Access Boundaries\n\n1. **`ecs_execution_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com` (and no other service or wildcard principal).\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**: CloudWatch Logs stream creation/writing (`logs:CreateLogStream`, `logs:PutLogEvents`, `logs:DescribeLogStreams`) scoped strictly to `logs.api_log_group`.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not allow, and must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"`, any SQS actions (`sqs:SendMessage`, `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`) on the main queue or DLQ, any DynamoDB actions (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteItem`, `dynamodb:Query`) on the projection table or `AccountIndex`, any S3 actions (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:ListBucket`) on the audit bucket (`<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`), `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on all four KMS keys (`database`, `messaging`, `projection`, `audit`), and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on the three non-API CloudWatch Log Groups (`projector`, `relay`, `archiver`).\n2. **`ecs_task_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com`.\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**:\n     - Publish-only access on the main SQS queue ARN (`sqs:SendMessage`, `sqs:GetQueueAttributes`, `sqs:GetQueueUrl`).\n     - Read-only access on the projection DynamoDB table ARN and its specific `AccountIndex` GSI ARN `<table_arn>/index/AccountIndex` (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:Query`, `dynamodb:DescribeTable`; do not use `<table_arn>/index/*` or `<table_arn>/*` wildcards).\n     - Cryptographic usage (`kms:Decrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:DescribeKey`) on the `messaging` and `projection` KMS key ARNs only.\n     - CloudWatch Logs stream creation/writing scoped strictly to `logs.api_log_group`.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not allow, and must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"`, consuming or deleting SQS messages (`sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`) on the main queue or `sqs:SendMessage`/`sqs:ReceiveMessage`/`sqs:DeleteMessage` on the DLQ; mutating DynamoDB (`dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteTable`) on the projection table; any S3 access (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:ListBucket`) on `<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`; `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on the `database` and `audit` KMS keys; and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on any non-API log group (`projector`, `relay`, `archiver`). Furthermore, must not grant `dynamodb:Query` on `<table_arn>/index/*`.\n3. **`projector_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `lambda.amazonaws.com`.\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**:\n     - Consume-only access on the main SQS queue ARN (`sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`, `sqs:GetQueueAttributes`, `sqs:ChangeMessageVisibility`) and dead-letter forwarding (`sqs:SendMessage`) on the DLQ ARN.\n     - Append/monotonic-upsert access on the projection DynamoDB table ARN and its specific `AccountIndex` GSI ARN `<table_arn>/index/AccountIndex` (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:Query`; do not use `<table_arn>/index/*` or `<table_arn>/*` wildcards).\n     - Cryptographic usage (`kms:Decrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:DescribeKey`) on the `messaging` and `projection` KMS key ARNs only.\n     - CloudWatch Logs stream creation/writing scoped strictly to `logs.projector_log_group`.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not allow, and must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"`, `sqs:SendMessage` on the main queue or `sqs:ReceiveMessage`/`sqs:DeleteMessage` on the DLQ; deleting DynamoDB items (`dynamodb:DeleteItem`) or tables (`dynamodb:DeleteTable`) on the projection table; any S3 access (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:ListBucket`) on `<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`; `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on the `database` and `audit` KMS keys; and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on any non-projector log group (`api`, `relay`, `archiver`). Furthermore, must not grant `dynamodb:Query` on `<table_arn>/index/*`.\n4. **`relay_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `lambda.amazonaws.com`.\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**:\n     - Publish-only access on the main SQS queue ARN (`sqs:SendMessage`, `sqs:GetQueueAttributes`, `sqs:GetQueueUrl`).\n     - Cryptographic usage (`kms:Decrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:DescribeKey`) on the `messaging` and `database` KMS key ARNs only.\n     - CloudWatch Logs stream creation/writing scoped strictly to `logs.relay_log_group`.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not allow, and must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"`, `sqs:ReceiveMessage` or `sqs:DeleteMessage` on the main queue, `sqs:SendMessage`/`sqs:ReceiveMessage`/`sqs:DeleteMessage` on the DLQ, any DynamoDB actions (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteItem`, `dynamodb:Query`) on the projection table or `AccountIndex`, any S3 actions (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:ListBucket`) on `<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`, `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on the `projection` and `audit` KMS keys, and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on any non-relay log group (`api`, `projector`, `archiver`).\n5. **`archiver_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `lambda.amazonaws.com`.\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**:\n     - Append-only object access (`s3:PutObject`, `s3:GetObject`, `s3:AbortMultipartUpload`) scoped strictly to `<audit_bucket_arn>/ledger-audit/*`, and bucket-level metadata (`s3:ListBucket`, `s3:GetBucketLocation`) scoped strictly to `<audit_bucket_arn>` (keep object-level and bucket-level statements separated by resource type).\n     - Cryptographic usage (`kms:Decrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:DescribeKey`) on the `audit` and `database` KMS key ARNs only.\n     - CloudWatch Logs stream creation/writing scoped strictly to `logs.archiver_log_group`.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not grant `s3:PutObject` on the bucket ARN `<audit_bucket_arn>` or unscoped `<audit_bucket_arn>/*` root wildcard, and must not grant `s3:ListBucket` on object ARNs. Must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"` `s3:DeleteObject` and `s3:DeleteObjectVersion` on `<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`, any SQS actions (`sqs:SendMessage`, `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`) on the main queue or DLQ, any DynamoDB actions (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteItem`, `dynamodb:Query`) on the projection table or `AccountIndex`, `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on the `messaging` and `projection` KMS keys, and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on any non-archiver log group (`api`, `projector`, `relay`).\n6. **`scheduler_role_arn`**:\n   - **Trust principal**: `scheduler.amazonaws.com`.\n   - **Allowed access (`Effect = \"Allow\"`)**:\n     - `lambda:InvokeFunction` scoped strictly to the Outbox Relay (`workers.outbox_relay.function_arn`) and Audit Archiver (`workers.audit_archiver.function_arn`) Lambda function ARNs.\n   - **Forbidden access (`Effect = \"Deny\"` required)**: Must not allow, and must explicitly deny via `Effect = \"Deny\"`, `lambda:InvokeFunction` on the Projector Lambda (`workers.projector.function_arn`), any SQS actions (`sqs:SendMessage`, `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`) on the main queue or DLQ, any DynamoDB actions (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, `dynamodb:DeleteItem`, `dynamodb:Query`) on the projection table or `AccountIndex`, any S3 actions (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:ListBucket`) on `<audit_bucket_arn>` and `<audit_bucket_arn>/*`, `kms:Decrypt` or `kms:GenerateDataKey` on all four KMS keys (`database`, `messaging`, `projection`, `audit`), and `logs:CreateLogStream` or `logs:PutLogEvents` on all four CloudWatch Log Groups (`api`, `projector`, `relay`, `archiver`).\n=== kms.md\n# Customer-Managed KMS Keys (`services/kms.md`)\n\nProvision four separate customer-managed KMS keys (`aws_kms_key`) and four KMS aliases (`aws_kms_alias`):\n\n- `kms.database_arn` with alias `alias/<resource_prefix>-database`: encrypts the RDS PostgreSQL instance\n- `kms.messaging_arn` with alias `alias/<resource_prefix>-messaging`: encrypts the main SQS queue and DLQ\n- `kms.projection_arn` with alias `alias/<resource_prefix>-projection`: encrypts the DynamoDB projection table\n- `kms.audit_arn` with alias `alias/<resource_prefix>-audit`: encrypts the S3 audit archive bucket\n\nEach of the four KMS keys must be configured with:\n- `enable_key_rotation = true`\n- `deletion_window_in_days = 10` (must be `10..30` days)\n- Tags `ClearLedgerDeployment = <resource_prefix>` and `ClearLedgerKeyUsage = <database|messaging|projection|audit>` (matching its respective role: `database`, `messaging`, `projection`, or `audit`)\n\n=== lambda.md\n# Lambda Workers and Event Source Mapping (`services/lambda.md`)\n\nProvision three container-based AWS Lambda functions (`aws_lambda_function`, `package_type = \"Image\"`):\n\n1. **Projector (`workers.projector`)**:\n   - `image_uri = projector_image` from `config.json`\n   - `role = iam.projector_role_arn`\n   - Environment variables: `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, `PROJECTION_TABLE`, `VALKEY_URL`, `CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP`\n   - Wired to the main SQS queue via an `aws_lambda_event_source_mapping` with:\n     - `enabled = true`\n     - `batch_size = 5`\n     - `maximum_batching_window_in_seconds = 0`\n     - `function_response_types = [\"ReportBatchItemFailures\"]`\n2. **Outbox Relay (`workers.outbox_relay`)**:\n   - `image_uri = relay_image` from `config.json`\n   - `role = iam.relay_role_arn`\n   - Environment variables: `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, `DATABASE_URL`, `SQS_QUEUE_URL`, `OUTBOX_BATCH_SIZE = \"50\"`, `CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP`\n3. **Audit Archiver (`workers.audit_archiver`)**:\n   - `image_uri = archiver_image` from `config.json`\n   - `role = iam.archiver_role_arn`\n   - Environment variables: `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, `DATABASE_URL`, `AUDIT_BUCKET`, `AUDIT_PREFIX = \"ledger-audit/\"`, `CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP`\n=== rds.md\n# RDS PostgreSQL (`services/rds.md`)\n\n- Provision a DB subnet group (`aws_db_subnet_group`) spanning strictly the private subnets (`network.private_subnet_ids`).\n- Provision a single PostgreSQL 16 RDS instance (`aws_db_instance`) with:\n  - `engine = \"postgres\"`\n  - `engine_version = \"16.3\"` (or `16.*`)\n  - `instance_class = \"db.t4g.micro\"`\n  - `db_name`, `username`, and `password` from `/workspace/config/config.json`\n  - `storage_encrypted = true`\n  - `kms_key_id` set to the customer-managed `database` KMS key ARN (`kms.database_arn`)\n  - `publicly_accessible = false`\n  - `skip_final_snapshot = true`\n  - `vpc_security_group_ids` containing the `rds` security group\n- Re-running `deploy.sh` must never replace the RDS instance or lose committed data.\n\n## Required Database Schema, Relational Invariants, and Triggers\n\nThe pre-built Rust binaries (`clearledger-api`, `clearledger-outbox-relay`, and `clearledger-audit-archiver`) do **not** run database migrations on startup. `clearledger-api` relies on PostgreSQL `CHECK`/`UNIQUE`/`FOREIGN KEY` constraints and PL/pgSQL triggers to enforce domain, schema, and state-transition invariants at the database layer (mapping SQLSTATE `23514`, `23503`, `23502`, `23505`, and `P0001` exceptions to HTTP `400 Bad Request`), and `GET /health/ready` verifies that all four tables, all three indexes, and user-defined triggers on all four tables exist in the `clearledger` schema before reporting `checks.postgres = \"UP\"`.\n\n`deploy.sh` must idempotently initialize the `clearledger` schema, all four tables, their constraints, their triggers, and all three indexes on the RDS PostgreSQL instance, and ensure that all user-defined triggers on all four tables are enabled (`tgenabled = 'O'`, re-enabling any trigger disabled out-of-band via `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE TRIGGER ALL`).\n\n### 1. Table `clearledger.settlements`\n\n- **Columns**:\n  - `settlement_id UUID NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY`\n  - `account_id TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `reference TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `debit_party TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `credit_party TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `current_status TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `current_stage TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `last_entry_id UUID NULL`\n  - `last_memo TEXT NULL`\n  - `version INTEGER NOT NULL`\n  - `entry_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`\n  - `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`\n  - `updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`\n- **Required invariants (enforced via `CHECK` constraints and `BEFORE UPDATE`/`BEFORE DELETE` triggers)**:\n  - Canonical trimmed strings and length bounds: `account_id`, `reference`, `debit_party`, `credit_party`, and `current_stage` (plus `last_memo` when non-null) must be stored in canonical trimmed form (`col = btrim(col)`, no leading or trailing whitespace) and match the length bounds and allowed status values of `CreateSettlementRequest` and `AppendEntryRequest` in `openapi.yaml` (including `1..256` characters when `last_memo` is non-null), with `debit_party <> credit_party` and `version >= 1`.\n  - At initiation (`version = 1`), `entry_count = 0`, `current_status = 'INITIATED'`, `current_stage = 'INITIATED@' || debit_party`, `last_entry_id IS NULL`, `last_memo = 'Settlement initiated'`, and `updated_at = created_at`. For `version > 1`, `entry_count = version - 1`, `current_status <> 'INITIATED'`, `last_entry_id IS NOT NULL`, and `updated_at > created_at`.\n  - On `UPDATE`: header columns (`settlement_id`, `account_id`, `reference`, `debit_party`, `credit_party`, `created_at`) are immutable; each update must step `version` and `entry_count` by `+1` with a new `last_entry_id` (`NEW.last_entry_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.last_entry_id`) and a strictly increasing `updated_at` timestamp (`NEW.updated_at > OLD.updated_at`); and `current_status` must follow the clearing lifecycle progression:\n    - The non-`DISPUTED` clearing status rank order is `INITIATED` (`0`) < `VALIDATED` (`1`) < `RESERVED` (`2`) < `CLEARED` (`3`) < `SETTLED` (`4`) < `RECONCILED` (`5`).\n    - `RECONCILED` is strictly terminal: once `OLD.current_status = 'RECONCILED'`, any `UPDATE` on the settlement row must be rejected (even if `NEW.current_status = 'RECONCILED'`).\n    - From any non-`RECONCILED`, non-`DISPUTED` status (`INITIATED`, `VALIDATED`, `RESERVED`, `CLEARED`, `SETTLED`), `NEW.current_status` may transition to `'DISPUTED'` or to any status whose rank is monotonic non-decreasing (`rank(NEW.current_status) >= rank(OLD.current_status)` — permitting same-status updates such as `CLEARED` -> `CLEARED` and single- or multi-stage forward advances such as `INITIATED` -> `VALIDATED` or `INITIATED` -> `CLEARED`, while rejecting any backward rank regression where `rank(NEW.current_status) < rank(OLD.current_status)` such as `CLEARED` -> `RESERVED`).\n    - From `OLD.current_status = 'DISPUTED'`, `NEW.current_status` may only remain `'DISPUTED'` or resolve to terminal `'RECONCILED'`.\n  - `clearledger.settlements` is an append-only ledger aggregate root (`DELETE` must be rejected).\n\n### 2. Table `clearledger.events`\n\n- **Columns**:\n  - `seq BIGSERIAL NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY`\n  - `event_id UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE`\n  - `settlement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES clearledger.settlements(settlement_id) ON DELETE CASCADE`\n  - `aggregate_version INTEGER NOT NULL`\n  - `event_type TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `correlation_id TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `idempotency_key TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL`\n  - `payload JSONB NOT NULL`\n  - `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`\n- **Required invariants (enforced via `UNIQUE`/`CHECK` constraints and `BEFORE INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` triggers)**:\n  - Composite `UNIQUE (settlement_id, aggregate_version)` and `UNIQUE (settlement_id, idempotency_key)`, with canonical trimmed storage (`col = btrim(col)`) and length bounds on `correlation_id` and `idempotency_key` matching `openapi.yaml`.\n  - `payload` must conform strictly to `ClearLedgerDomainEventEnvelope` in `schemas/events.schema.json` (including `additionalProperties: false` on both the envelope and `payload.data`, required non-null canonically trimmed `accountId`, `reference`, `debitParty`, `creditParty`, `status`, and `clearingStage` in `payload.data` with length bounds matching `openapi.yaml` and `1..256` canonically trimmed characters when `data.memo` is non-null, column-to-envelope equality across `event_id`, `settlement_id`, `aggregate_version`, `event_type`, `correlation_id`, `idempotency_key`, and `occurred_at` compared as `TIMESTAMPTZ`, and version/kind/status/entryId coupling for `SettlementInitiated` at `v = 1` with `data.clearingStage = 'INITIATED@' || (data.debitParty)` and `data.memo = 'Settlement initiated'` vs `LedgerEntryRecorded` at `v >= 2`).\n  - On `INSERT`: per-settlement `aggregate_version` must be contiguous starting at `1`; `data.entryId` must be unique per settlement across all `LedgerEntryRecorded` events; the event must match the parent row in `clearledger.settlements` (including header fields, `current_status`, `current_stage`, `last_entry_id`, `last_memo`, `version`, and `occurred_at = updated_at`, plus `occurred_at = created_at` at `v = 1`); and for `aggregate_version >= 2`, `NEW.occurred_at` must be strictly greater (`>`) than the immediately preceding event's `occurred_at` (`aggregate_version = NEW.aggregate_version - 1`) and the status transition from that preceding event's `data.status` to `NEW.payload->'data'->>'status'` must satisfy the settlement status transition rules above (monotonic non-decreasing rank, reachable `DISPUTED` from non-`RECONCILED`, `DISPUTED` only to `DISPUTED` or `RECONCILED`, and no transitions out of or repeating `RECONCILED`).\n  - `clearledger.events` is strictly append-only (`UPDATE` and `DELETE` must be rejected).\n\n### 3. Table `clearledger.outbox`\n\n- **Columns**:\n  - `seq BIGSERIAL NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY`\n  - `event_id UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES clearledger.events(event_id) ON DELETE CASCADE`\n  - `settlement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES clearledger.settlements(settlement_id) ON DELETE CASCADE`\n  - `aggregate_version INTEGER NOT NULL`\n  - `correlation_id TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `payload JSONB NOT NULL`\n  - `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`\n  - `published_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`\n  - `archived_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`\n  - `attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`\n  - `last_error TEXT NULL`\n- **Required invariants (enforced via `UNIQUE`/`FOREIGN KEY`/`CHECK` constraints and triggers)**:\n  - Composite `UNIQUE (settlement_id, aggregate_version)` and `FOREIGN KEY (settlement_id, aggregate_version) REFERENCES clearledger.events(settlement_id, aggregate_version) ON DELETE CASCADE`, with canonical trimmed `correlation_id` (`correlation_id = btrim(correlation_id)`).\n  - `payload` must conform to `ClearLedgerDomainEventEnvelope` (`schemas/events.schema.json`) and on `INSERT` must exactly mirror the corresponding row in `clearledger.events` in contiguous per-settlement `aggregate_version` order starting at `1`.\n  - Delivery/archival lifecycle: `attempts >= 0`; when `attempts = 0`, both `published_at` and `last_error` must be `NULL`; when `published_at IS NOT NULL`, `attempts >= 1`, `last_error IS NULL`, and `published_at >= created_at`; when `last_error IS NOT NULL`, `published_at IS NULL`, `attempts >= 1`, `length(btrim(last_error)) > 0`, and `last_error = btrim(last_error)`; `archived_at` requires `published_at IS NOT NULL` and `archived_at >= published_at`.\n  - `DELETE` is forbidden; on `UPDATE`, envelope columns are immutable, `attempts` cannot decrease, publishing an unpublished row requires incrementing `attempts` with `archived_at IS NULL`, while `published_at` remains `NOT NULL` (such as during archival or resetting `archived_at = NULL` for S3 re-archival), `published_at`, `attempts`, and `last_error` cannot be mutated (resetting `published_at = NULL, archived_at = NULL` for operational replay is permitted), and once `OLD.archived_at IS NOT NULL` and `NEW.archived_at IS NOT NULL`, `NEW.archived_at` cannot be mutated to a different timestamp without first resetting `archived_at = NULL`.\n\n### 4. Table `clearledger.idempotency_keys`\n\n- **Columns**:\n  - `scope TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `idempotency_key TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `request_hash TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `status_code INTEGER NOT NULL`\n  - `response_body JSONB NOT NULL`\n  - `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`\n  - Composite `PRIMARY KEY (scope, idempotency_key)`\n- **Required invariants (enforced via `CHECK` constraints and triggers)**:\n  - `scope` (`create:<settlement_uuid>` or `entry:<settlement_uuid>`), canonically trimmed `idempotency_key` (`idempotency_key = btrim(idempotency_key)` and `8..128` chars), lowercase hex SHA-256 `request_hash`, `status_code` (`201` for `create:*` at `version = 1`; `202` for `entry:*` at `version >= 2`), and closed-schema `response_body` (`WriteAcceptedResponse` in `openapi.yaml` with `accepted = true` and `idempotentReplay = false`).\n  - On `INSERT`, the referenced event (`eventId`, `settlementId`, `version`, `idempotency_key`) must exist in both `clearledger.events` and `clearledger.outbox`, and each `response_body->>'eventId'` (as well as each `(response_body->>'settlementId', (response_body->>'version')::integer)` pair) must be unique across `clearledger.idempotency_keys`. `UPDATE` and `DELETE` must be rejected.\n\n### 5. Required Indexes in `clearledger` Schema\n\n- `idx_clearledger_outbox_unpublished`: on `clearledger.outbox (seq)` with partial predicate `WHERE published_at IS NULL`\n- `idx_clearledger_outbox_unarchived`: on `clearledger.outbox (seq)` with partial predicate `WHERE published_at IS NOT NULL AND archived_at IS NULL`\n- `idx_clearledger_events_settlement_version`: on `clearledger.events (settlement_id, aggregate_version)`\n=== s3.md\n# S3 Audit Archive (`services/s3.md`)\n\n- Provision a dedicated S3 bucket (`aws_s3_bucket`) for NDJSON audit batches (`force_destroy = true` recommended so `destroy.sh` can remove the bucket after versioned audit objects and delete markers are written).\n- Enable bucket versioning (`aws_s3_bucket_versioning` with `status = \"Enabled\"`).\n- Enable default server-side encryption (`aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration`) using `sse_algorithm = \"aws:kms\"` and `kms_master_key_id = kms.audit_arn`.\n- Block all public access (`aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block`) with all four flags (`block_public_acls`, `block_public_policy`, `ignore_public_acls`, `restrict_public_buckets`) set to `true`.\n- Configure the Audit Archiver Lambda with `AUDIT_BUCKET = <bucket_name>` and `AUDIT_PREFIX = \"ledger-audit/\"` (`manifest.audit.prefix = \"ledger-audit/\"`).\n- `clearledger-audit-archiver` writes NDJSON batches to `s3://<bucket_name>/ledger-audit/batch-<first_seq:08d>-<last_seq:08d>-<16_char_sha256_hex>.ndjson`, where `<first_seq:08d>` and `<last_seq:08d>` are the 8-digit zero-padded first and last `clearledger.outbox.seq` in the batch, each batch contains a contiguous, gap-free slice of all committed `clearledger.outbox` rows whose `seq` lies in `[first_seq, last_seq]` ordered by strictly ascending `clearledger.outbox.seq`, batch `[first_seq, last_seq]` intervals are strictly disjoint and non-overlapping across objects, and `<16_char_sha256_hex>` is the first 16 lowercase hexadecimal Table `clearledger.settlements`\n\n- **Columns**:\n  - `settlement_id UUID NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY`\n  - `account_id TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `reference TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `debit_party TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `credit_party TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `current_status TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `current_stage TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `last_entry_id UUID NULL`\n  - `last_memo TEXT NULL`\n  - `version INTEGER NOT NULL`\n  - `entry_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`\n  - `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`\n  - `updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`\n- **Required invariants (enforced via `CHECK` constraints and `BEFORE UPDATE`/`BEFORE DELETE` triggers)**:\n  - Canonical trimmed strings and length bounds: `account_id`, `reference`, `debit_party`, `credit_party`, and `current_stage` (plus `last_memo` when non-null) must be stored in canonical trimmed form (`col = btrim(col)`, no leading or trailing whitespace) and match the length bounds and allowed status values of `CreateSettlementRequest` and `AppendEntryRequest` in `openapi.yaml` (including `1..256` characters when `last_memo` is non-null), with `debit_party <> credit_party` and `version >= 1`.\n  - At initiation (`version = 1`), `entry_count = 0`, `current_status = 'INITIATED'`, `current_stage = 'INITIATED@' || debit_party`, `last_entry_id IS NULL`, `last_memo = 'Settlement initiated'`, and `updated_at = created_at`. For `version > 1`, `entry_count = version - 1`, `current_status <> 'INITIATED'`, `last_entry_id IS NOT NULL`, and `updated_at > created_at`.\n  - On `UPDATE`: header columns (`settlement_id`, `account_id`, `reference`, `debit_party`, `credit_party`, `created_at`) are immutable; each update must step `version` and `entry_count` by `+1` with a new `last_entry_id` (`NEW.last_entry_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.last_entry_id`) and a strictly increasing `updated_at` timestamp (`NEW.updated_at > OLD.updated_at`); and `current_status` must follow the clearing lifecycle progression:\n    - The non-`DISPUTED` clearing status rank order is `INITIATED` (`0`) < `VALIDATED` (`1`) < `RESERVED` (`2`) < `CLEARED` (`3`) < `SETTLED` (`4`) < `RECONCILED` (`5`).\n    - `RECONCILED` is strictly terminal: once `OLD.current_status = 'RECONCILED'`, any `UPDATE` on the settlement row must be rejected (even if `NEW.current_status = 'RECONCILED'`).\n    - From any non-`RECONCILED`, non-`DISPUTED` status (`INITIATED`, `VALIDATED`, `RESERVED`, `CLEARED`, `SETTLED`), `NEW.current_status` may transition to `'DISPUTED'` or to any status whose rank is monotonic non-decreasing (`rank(NEW.current_status) >= rank(OLD.current_status)` — permitting same-status updates such as `CLEARED` -> `CLEARED` and single- or multi-stage forward advances such as `INITIATED` -> `VALIDATED` or `INITIATED` -> `CLEARED`, while rejecting any backward rank regression where `rank(NEW.current_status) < rank(OLD.current_status)` such as `CLEARED` -> `RESERVED`).\n    - From `OLD.current_status = 'DISPUTED'`, `NEW.current_status` may only remain `'DISPUTED'` or resolve to terminal `'RECONCILED'`.\n  - `clearledger.settlements` is an append-only ledger aggregate root (`DELETE` must be rejected).\n\n### 2. Table `clearledger.events`\n\n- **Columns**:\n  - `seq BIGSERIAL NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY`\n  - `event_id UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE`\n  - `settlement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES clearledger.settlements(settlement_id) ON DELETE CASCADE`\n  - `aggregate_version INTEGER NOT NULL`\n  - `event_type TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `correlation_id TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `idempotency_key TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL`\n  - `payload JSONB NOT NULL`\n  - `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`\n- **Required invariants (enforced via `UNIQUE`/`CHECK` constraints and `BEFORE INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` triggers)**:\n  - Composite `UNIQUE (settlement_id, aggregate_version)` and `UNIQUE (settlement_id, idempotency_key)`, with canonical trimmed storage (`col = btrim(col)`) and length bounds on `correlation_id` and `idempotency_key` matching `openapi.yaml`.\n  - `payload` must conform strictly to `ClearLedgerDomainEventEnvelope` in `schemas/events.schema.json` (including `additionalProperties: false` on both the envelope and `payload.data`, required non-null canonically trimmed `accountId`, `reference`, `debitParty`, `creditParty`, `status`, and `clearingStage` in `payload.data` with length bounds matching `openapi.yaml` and `1..256` canonically trimmed characters when `data.memo` is non-null, column-to-envelope equality across `event_id`, `settlement_id`, `aggregate_version`, `event_type`, `correlation_id`, `idempotency_key`, and `occurred_at` compared as `TIMESTAMPTZ`, and version/kind/status/entryId coupling for `SettlementInitiated` at `v = 1` with `data.clearingStage = 'INITIATED@' || (data.debitParty)` and `data.memo = 'Settlement initiated'` vs `LedgerEntryRecorded` at `v >= 2`).\n  - On `INSERT`: per-settlement `aggregate_version` must be contiguous starting at `1`; Table `clearledger.outbox`\n\n- **Columns**:\n  - `seq BIGSERIAL NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY`\n  - `event_id UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES clearledger.events(event_id) ON DELETE CASCADE`\n  - `settlement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES clearledger.settlements(settlement_id) ON DELETE CASCADE`\n  - `aggregate_version INTEGER NOT NULL`\n  - `correlation_id TEXT NOT NULL`\n  - `payload JSONB NOT NULL`\n  - `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`\n  - `published_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`\n  - `archived_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`\n  - `attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`\n  - `last_error TEXT NULL`\n- **Required invariants (enforced via `UNIQUE`/`FOREIGN KEY`/`CHECK` constraints and triggers)**:\n  - Composite `UNIQUE (settlement_id, aggregate_version)` and `FOREIGN KEY (settlement_id, aggregate_version) REFERENCES clearledger.events(settlement_id, aggregate_version) ON DELETE CASCADE`, with canonical trimmed `correlation_id` (`correlation_id = btrim(correlation_id)`).\n  - `payload` must conform to `ClearLedgerDomainEventEnvelope` (`schemas/events.schema.json`) and on `INSERT` must exactly mirror the corresponding row in `clearledger.events` in contiguous per-settlement `aggregate_version` order starting at `1`.\n  - Delivery/archival lifecycle: `attempts >= 0`; when `attempts = 0`, both `published_at` and `last_error` must be `NULL`; when `published_at IS NOT NULL`, `attempts >= 1`, `last_error IS NULL`, and `published_at >= created_at`; when `last_error IS NOT NULL`, `published_at IS NULL`, `attempts >= 1`, `length(btrim(last_error)) > 0`, and `last_error = btrim(last_error)`; `archived_at` requires `published_at IS NOT NULL` and `archived_at >= published_at`.\n  - `DELETE` is forbidden; on `UPDATE`, envelope columns are immutable, `attempts` cannot decrease, publishing an unpublished row requires incrementing `attempts` with `archived_at IS NULL`, while `published_at` remains `NOT NULL` (such as during archival or resetting `archived_at = NULL` for S3 re-archival), `published_at`, `attempts`, and `last_error` cannot be mutated (resetting `published_at = NULL, archived_at = NULL` for operational replay is permitted), and once `OLD.archived_at IS NOT NULL` and `NEW.archived_at IS NOT NULL`, `NEW.archived_at` cannot be mutated to a different timestamp without first resetting `archived_at = NULL`.\n\n### 4. A failed restore does not release or renumber a reserved endpoint; a retry\nor the next boot uses the same port.\nThis recoverable emulator condition uses `available`, the same metadata-only status as a\nrestart without a reachable Docker daemon, not AWS's terminal `failed` state. No RDS event reaches SNS\nthrough it, so an SNS subscriber sees nothing.\n\n`SourceIds` is set at create and changed only through `AddSourceIdentifierToSubscription` and\n`RemoveSourceIdentifierFromSubscription`, since `ModifyEventSubscription` carries no `SourceIds`\nmember. For private registry authentication and other Docker settings see [Docker Configuration](../configuration/docker.md).\n\n`CreateDBInstance`, `CreateDBCluster`, `RestoreDBInstanceFromDBSnapshot`,\n`RestoreDBClusterFromSnapshot` and the two point in time restores honor a requested `Port` only within the configured\nRDS proxy range. A port outside that range causes Floci to assign the next free port\nand return it in the endpoint. A port inside the range that is already in use is\nrejected. This differs from AWS because Floci's local proxy must use a published\nhost port; for example, requesting `5432` with the default\n`7001`-`7099` range returns a port in that range. Ports outside AWS's valid\n`1150`-`65535` interval are rejected.\n\nWhen Docker publishes RDS proxy ports dynamically, set `FLOCI_SERVICES_RDS_ENDPOINT_HOST` to the\nhostname used by clients. Floci inspects its own container through the Docker socket and returns the\ncorresponding published port from `DescribeDBInstances` and `DescribeDBClusters`. Leave the setting\nunset to retain the auto-detected endpoint host and configured proxy port.\n\n```yaml\nservices:\n  floci:\n    image: floci/floci:latest\n    ports:\n      - \"4566:4566\"\n      - \"7001-7099:7001-7099\"   # RDS proxy ports\n    volumes:\n      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock\n    environment:\n      FLOCI_SERVICES_DOCKER_NETWORK: my-project_default\n      FLOCI_SERVICES_RDS_PROXY_BASE_PORT: \"7001\"\n```\n\n### Without a reachable Docker daemon\n\nA DB instance or cluster record is metadata. Its identifier, ARN, endpoint address and tags come\nfrom Floci's configuration, not from Docker. When no daemon is reachable, because Floci runs inside\nDocker with no socket mounted or the daemon on the host is stopped, `CreateDBInstance` and\n`CreateDBCluster` still succeed and the resource reaches `available`. `DescribeDBInstances`,\n`ModifyDBInstance`, the tagging APIs and `DeleteDBInstance` all work on that record, and Floci logs\na warning naming the missing daemon.\n\nNothing listens behind the endpoint in that state. The backing container is retried by every\noperation that needs the live database, so it starts as soon as a daemon becomes reachable. Until\nthen, RDS Data API calls fail with a modelled `InternalServerErrorException` that names the missing\ndaemon. A daemon that is reachable but cannot start the container still fails `CreateDBInstance`\noutright, since that is a real error rather than a degraded mode.\n\n### Mock mode (CI / tests)\n\nSet `FLOCI_SERVICES_RDS_MOCK=true` when you only need the management API shape: clusters and\ninstances are registered as `available` immediately, with no Docker container or auth proxy behind\nthem. Each resource still gets a unique endpoint port, but nothing listens on it.\n\n```yaml\n# docker-compose.yml — CI / test environment\nservices:\n  floci:\n    image: floci/floci:latest\n    environment:\n      FLOCI_SERVICES_RDS_MOCK: \"true\"\n```\n\n!!! note \"Switching modes over persisted state\"\n    With a persistent storage mode, changing `FLOCI_SERVICES_RDS_MOCK` between restarts is\n    best-effort, as with the other mock-capable services: resources created in real mode and\n    deleted under mock leave their containers and volumes behind, and resources created in mock\n    mode are restored with fresh, empty containers when loaded in real mode.\n\n!!! warning \"DB proxy endpoint routing\"\n\n    DB proxy control-plane resources and target registration are modeled, but Floci's current\n    single-host TCP relay cannot expose multiple same-engine DB proxies as distinct AWS-style bare\n    hostnames on the same engine-default port. The standard Docker Compose mapping also exposes\n    only the `7001-7099` instance/cluster proxy range, not `1433`, `3306`, or `5432`. Use mock mode\n    for DB proxy provisioning workflows until a dedicated endpoint-routing design is implemented.\n\n!!! note \"DB proxy control-plane settings\"\n\n    Proxy and target-group settings are persisted and round-trip through the RDS Query API and\n    CloudFormation. Pool sizing, borrow timeout, idle timeout, TLS, init-query, and session-pinning\n    settings are currently control-plane metadata; the TCP relay does not yet implement those data-plane\n    behaviors. `DefaultAuthScheme=IAM_AUTH` is supported for control-plane workflows, but a real-mode\n    proxy using that scheme cannot register a target until backend IAM authentication is implemented.\n    Requests to `RegisterDBProxyTargets`, `DeregisterDBProxyTargets`, and\n    `DescribeDBProxyTargets` use the `default` target group when `TargetGroupName` is omitted,\n    matching the RDS API contract.\n    `CreateDBProxy`/`AWS::RDS::DBProxy` accept `EndpointNetworkType` (`IPV4`, `IPV6`, or `DUAL`) and\n    `TargetConnectionNetworkType` (`IPV4` or `IPV6`) and round-trip them like the other proxy\n    settings above; the TCP relay itself still only listens on IPv4, so a non-`IPV4` value is\n    accepted as control-plane metadata rather than making the relay dual-stack. A non-`IPV4` value\n    is rejected with `InvalidParameterValue` unless the proxy's VPC and every subnet in\n    `VpcSubnetIds` already carry an associated IPv6 CIDR block, matching AWS's own network\n    prerequisites for RDS Proxy.\n\n## Aurora Serverless v2 scaling\n\n`CreateDBCluster`, `ModifyDBCluster`, and `DescribeDBClusters` support the AWS\n`ServerlessV2ScalingConfiguration` Query shape for `aurora-mysql` and `aurora-postgresql`\nclusters. Requests that apply this configuration to another engine fail with\n`InvalidParameterCombination`.\n\nThe minimum and maximum capacities use half-ACU increments; the maximum must be at least 1 ACU and\nno greater than 256 ACUs. AWS's actual maximum depends on the Aurora engine and platform version,\nwhile Floci currently applies the 256-ACU ceiling uniformly.\n\nWhen `MinCapacity` is zero, `SecondsUntilAutoPause` accepts 300–86,400 seconds and defaults to 300.\nChanging the minimum to a nonzero value removes the auto-pause interval, matching the AWS response\nshape. AWS limits zero-capacity auto-pause to compatible Aurora versions; Floci does not currently\nenforce that version matrix. `ModifyDBCluster` accepts partial scaling updates and preserves omitted\nvalues. `AWS::RDS::DBCluster` creation also maps the equivalent CloudFormation property.\n\nIf a persisted cluster record does not contain its original AWS engine identifier, Floci rejects a\nnew scaling configuration instead of assuming that the cluster is Aurora.\n\nFloci persists and returns the scaling configuration but does not resize the backing Docker\ncontainer: capacity between `MinCapacity` and `MaxCapacity` is not modeled. A `MinCapacity` of 0\ndoes take effect, as described next.\n\n### Automatic pause and resume\n\nA cluster whose `MinCapacity` is 0 pauses the way Aurora Serverless v2 does. Once nothing has used\nit for `SecondsUntilAutoPause`, Floci freezes its database container with `docker pause`, which\nkeeps its data and its endpoint. The next connection resumes it: the client is held, not refused,\nuntil the database runs again, and is then served as usual. As on AWS, a connection attempt with\nwrong credentials also resumes the cluster.\n\n- **What keeps a cluster awake.** Every open connection through the cluster endpoint, the reader\n  endpoint, an instance endpoint or an RDS Proxy, every RDS Data API call and every open Data API\n  transaction. The idle clock starts when the last of them ends.\n- **Which clusters pause.** Aurora PostgreSQL and Aurora MySQL clusters with at least one instance,\n  all of them `db.serverless` and available. As on AWS, a cluster with a provisioned instance, a\n  cluster in a global database and a cluster registered with an RDS Proxy stay running. Floci runs\n  a cluster's instances in one container, so they pause and resume together, like Aurora's writer\n  and its tier 0 and 1 readers; a reader in tiers 2 to 15 does not pause on its own.\n- **What you can observe.** The cluster `Status` and each `DBInstanceStatus` stay `available`.\n  `DescribeEvents` reports RDS-EVENT-0370 to 0374 for each instance, for example \"Successfully\n  paused the DB instance.\". While the cluster is paused, `ServerlessDatabaseCapacity` reports 0\n  and `ACUUtilization` and `CPUUtilization` report 0 percent in the `AWS/RDS` namespace once a\n  minute, by `DBClusterIdentifier` and by `DBInstanceIdentifier`. Floci publishes none of them\n  while the cluster runs.\n- **Resume delay.** Aurora takes about 15 seconds to resume. Floci resumes at once unless\n  `FLOCI_SERVICES_RDS_AURORA_RESUME_DELAY_MILLIS` is set; `15000` exercises client connect timeouts,\n  retries and connection-pool validation against a realistic cold start.\n- **Configuration changes.** A `ModifyDBCluster` that raises `MinCapacity` above 0 or changes\n  `SecondsUntilAutoPause` resumes a paused cluster and restarts its idle clock.\n- **Commands Floci runs in the container.** `CreateDBClusterSnapshot` and a master password change\n  run inside the database container, so they resume a paused cluster first. Aurora takes snapshots\n  from storage without resuming it.\n- Stopping, rebooting or deleting a cluster, restarting Floci and resetting its state never leave a\n  container frozen. A cluster that was paused when Floci stopped comes back running.\n- `FLOCI_SERVICES_RDS_AURORA_AUTO_PAUSE_ENABLED=false` keeps every cluster running.\n\nNot emulated: Data API requests to a paused cluster wait for the resume, as the Aurora user guide\ndescribes, and never fail with `DatabaseResumingException`; logical or binlog replication does not\nkeep a cluster awake; and parameter group changes do not resume one.\n\n## Modifying a DB instance\n\n`ModifyDBInstance` applies `DBInstanceClass`, `AllocatedStorage` and `EngineVersion`, and\n`DescribeDBInstances` reports the new values. Members the request leaves out keep their current\nvalue, so a partial modify does not reset anything.\n\n`AllocatedStorage` follows the AWS rules for the member:\n\n- A size smaller than the current one fails with `InvalidParameterCombination`. RDS storage never\n  shrinks.\n- On PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, an increase of less than 10% is rounded up to 10% greater\n  rather than refused, which is what AWS does. SQL Server takes the size it is given.\n- The same size is not a change and is left alone.\n\n`EngineVersion` accepts a minor upgrade on its own. A different major version needs\n`AllowMajorVersionUpgrade`, without which the request fails with `InvalidParameterCombination`.\nMajor versions are compared on the leading version component, so a MySQL 8.0 to 8.4 upgrade reads\nas a minor one here while AWS treats it as major.\n\nA refused member fails the whole request: a modify that carries a new `DBInstanceClass` alongside a\nshrinking `AllocatedStorage` returns `InvalidParameterCombination` and leaves the class as it was,\nso a read-back never reports a value the request did not get.\n\nTwo deviations are worth knowing:\n\n- **Changes apply immediately.** AWS defers a class, storage or engine-version change to the\n  preferred maintenance window unless `ApplyImmediately` is set, and reports it under\n  `PendingModifiedValues` until then. Floci runs no maintenance window and does not model\n  `PendingModifiedValues`, so it applies the change as soon as the request lands whatever\n  `ApplyImmediately` says. Without this a deferred change would never be applied at all, and every\n  read-back would report the same drift.\n- **The backing container is not re-imaged.** An engine-version change is recorded on the instance\n  and reported on read, but the container started at create time keeps running the image it was\n  started with. This is control-plane compatibility, like Aurora Serverless v2 scaling above.\n\n`StorageType`, `MultiAZ` and `Iops` are not read on a modify yet. Floci reports every instance as\n`gp2`.\n\n## Examples\n\n```bash\nexport AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localhost:4566\n\n# Create a PostgreSQL instance\naws rds create-db-instance \\\n  --db-instance-identifier mypostgres \\\n  --db-instance-class db.t3.micro \\\n  --engine postgres \\\n  --master-username admin \\\n  --master-user-password secret123 \\\n  --allocated-storage 20 \\\n  --endpoint-url $AWS_ENDPOINT_URL\n\n# Get connection details\naws rds describe-db-instances \\\n  --db-instance-identifier mypostgres \\\n  --query 'DBInstances[0].Endpoint' \\\n  --endpoint-url $AWS_ENDPOINT_URL\n\n# Connect with psql (use the port returned above)\npsql -h localhost -p 7001 -U admin\n\n# Create a MySQL instance\naws rds create-db-instance \\\n  --db-instance-identifier mymysql \\\n  --db-instance-class db.t3.micro \\\n  --engine mysql \\\n  --master-username root \\\n  --master-user-password secret123 \\\n  --allocated-storage 20 \\\n  --endpoint-url $AWS_ENDPOINT_URL\n\n# Connect with mysql client\nmysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 7002 -u root -psecret123\n```\n\n## Supported Engines\n\n| Engine | Default image |\n|---|---|\n| `postgres` | `postgres:16-alpine` |\n| `mysql` | `mysql:8.0` |\n| `mariadb` | `mariadb:11` |\n\nOverride the image per-instance with the `--engine-version` flag or globally via environment variables.\nAurora MySQL versions such as `8.0.mysql_aurora.3.08.0` use the MySQL version in front, so that example runs `mysql:8.0`.\n\n## Option Groups\n\nOption groups are metadata: Floci stores the options you add, returns them on the wire, and\nattaches a group to a DB instance, but it does not install the underlying engine feature in the\ncontainer.\n\nAs on AWS, every engine has an implicit `default:<engine>-<major version>` group that\n`DescribeOptionGroups` returns even when you have created none. Floci ships the defaults for the\nengines it can run (`postgres 13`–`18`, `mysql 8.0`/`8.4`, `mariadb 10.11`/`11.2`/`11.4`), so an\ninstance created without `--option-group-name` reports the matching default. Default groups can't\nbe modified, deleted, or tagged.\n\n`CreateOptionGroup` accepts any `EngineName` AWS accepts — including `oracle-*`, `sqlserver-*`,\nand `db2-*` — so a Terraform `aws_db_option_group` for an engine Floci cannot start still applies.\nAttaching one to a DB instance requires the group's engine and major engine version to match the\ninstance, as on AWS: a `mysql 8.0` group can't be attached to a `mysql 8.4` instance. A mismatch\nfails with `InvalidParameterCombination`.\n\n```bash\naws rds create-option-group \\\n  --option-group-name my-og \\\n  --engine-name mysql \\\n  --major-engine-version 8.0 \\\n  --option-group-description \"MySQL options\" \\\n  --endpoint-url $AWS_ENDPOINT_URL\n\naws rds modify-option-group \\\n  --option-group-name my-og \\\n  --options OptionName=MEMCACHED,Port=11211 \\\n  --apply-immediately \\\n  --endpoint-url $AWS_ENDPOINT_URL\n\naws rds describe-option-groups \\\n  --engine-name mysql \\\n  --endpoint-url $AWS_ENDPOINT_URL\n```\n\nDeleting a group that is still attached to a DB instance fails with\n`InvalidOptionGroupStateFault`, matching AWS.\n\nKnown gaps, all deliberate:\n\n| Behavior | Status |\n|---|---|\n| `DescribeOptionGroupOptions` | Not implemented: the per-engine option catalog is not modeled |\n| `OptionGroupQuotaExceededFault` (AWS caps an account at 20 groups) | Not enforced — capping a local emulator would only get in a test's way |\n| `OptionSetting` metadata (`DataType`, `ApplyType`, `AllowedValues`, `DefaultValue`, `Description`) | Omitted — it would require the per-engine option catalog `DescribeOptionGroupOptions` serves |\n| `MaxRecords` / `Marker` pagination | Every group is returned in one page, as with every other RDS list action |\n\n## Read replicas\n\n`CreateDBInstanceReadReplica` creates a standalone instance with its own container and endpoint.\nAs on AWS it inherits the source's engine, version, credentials and database name and, unless the\nrequest overrides them, the instance class, storage and minor version upgrade setting. A replica\nin the source's region also inherits the source's parameter group, option group, subnet group and\nsecurity groups; a replica in another region (source given by ARN, `--region` set to the\ndestination) gets that region's defaults. IAM authentication and `CopyTagsToSnapshot` are off\nunless requested. The replica starts with `BackupRetentionPeriod` 0. Both ends report the link\nthe way `DescribeDBInstances` does: the replica carries `ReadReplicaSourceDBInstanceIdentifier`\nand a `StatusInfos` entry of type `read replication`, the source lists it under\n`ReadReplicaDBInstanceIdentifiers`; within a region the link is the identifier, across regions\nit is the ARN. A `DBSubnetGroupName` with a source given by plain identifier is refused with\n`DBSubnetGroupNotAllowedFault`, as on AWS.\n\nThe replica's database is initialised from a `pg_dumpall` of the source taken when the replica is\ncreated, the same mechanism `RestoreDBInstanceFromDBSnapshot` uses, so it holds the source's data\nas of that moment. Writes made to the source afterwards are not streamed to the replica. Because\nthe copy is dump based, only PostgreSQL sources are accepted; MySQL and MariaDB sources are refused\nwith `InvalidDBInstanceState`, as `CreateDBSnapshot` refuses them. A source with automated backups\noff (`BackupRetentionPeriod` 0) is refused with the same error AWS uses.\n\n`PromoteReadReplica` clears the link on both ends, sets the requested `BackupRetentionPeriod`\n(one day when omitted) and `PreferredBackupWindow`, and reboots the instance as AWS does, so open\nconnections drop while the container, endpoint and data stay. Deleting a source promotes its\nsame-region replicas; a cross-region replica keeps its link with the replication status\n`terminated` until it is promoted or deleted, which is what AWS does for PostgreSQL. Deleting a\nreplica drops it from its source's list.\n\n## Cluster endpoints\n\n`CreateDBClusterEndpoint` adds an Aurora custom endpoint to an available cluster. As the Aurora user\nguide describes, its type is `READER` or `ANY` (case-insensitive, as the CLI sends it), it holds either\na static list or an exclusion list of the cluster's instances but not both\n(`InvalidParameterCombination`), and a `READER` endpoint cannot list the writer. A member that is not\nan instance of the cluster is `DBInstanceNotFound`. The identifier follows the RDS identifier rules\n(at most 63 characters), is stored lower case and is unique in the Region\n(`DBClusterEndpointAlreadyExistsFault`); a cluster holds at most five custom endpoints\n(`DBClusterEndpointQuotaExceededFault`). The endpoint's ARN,\n`arn:aws:rds:<region>:<account>:cluster-endpoint:<id>`, works with the tagging actions.\n\n`DescribeDBClusterEndpoints` lists each cluster's built-in `WRITER` and `READER` endpoints followed by\nits custom endpoints, narrowed by `DBClusterIdentifier`, `DBClusterEndpointIdentifier` and the filters\n`db-cluster-endpoint-type`, `db-cluster-endpoint-custom-type`, `db-cluster-endpoint-id` and\n`db-cluster-endpoint-status`. `ModifyDBClusterEndpoint` changes the type or replaces the member list\n(giving static members clears the exclusion list, and the other way round). Deleting a cluster deletes\nits custom endpoints, and a deleted instance drops out of the lists that name it.\n\nA `READER` endpoint leaves out the cluster's current writer, so after a failover the promoted\ninstance no longer shows among its members, as Aurora adjusts `READER` membership. Member names match\nthe cluster's instances regardless of case and are stored as the cluster spells them.\n\nCustom endpoints are modelled, not routed: a custom endpoint reports the cluster's own endpoint host\n(read from the cluster each time, so it follows a restart onto another proxy port), so it is\nreachable, but connections through it go where the cluster endpoint sends them rather than being\nspread across the chosen members.\n\n## Point in time restore\n\n`RestoreDBInstanceToPointInTime` and `RestoreDBClusterToPointInTime` check the request as AWS does:\nexactly one of `RestoreTime` (`RestoreToTime` for a cluster) and `UseLatestRestorableTime`, and a\ntime inside the source's restorable window, or `InvalidRestoreFault`. The window is what the describe\ncalls report. An instance's runs from the later of its creation and the start of its backup\nretention period up to `LatestRestorableTime` on `DescribeDBInstances`; an instance with\n`BackupRetentionPeriod` 0 reports no `LatestRestorableTime` and is refused with\n`PointInTimeRestoreNotEnabled`. Floci does not model a cluster's backup retention, so a cluster's\nwindow runs from its creation (`EarliestRestorableTime`) to `LatestRestorableTime` on\n`DescribeDBClusters`.\n\nAn instance source is named by `SourceDBInstanceIdentifier` or `SourceDbiResourceId`, a cluster\nsource by `SourceDBClusterIdentifier` (identifier or ARN) or `SourceDbClusterResourceId`. Restoring\nfrom retained automated backups (`SourceDBInstanceAutomatedBackupsArn`, used for a deleted instance)\nis not supported, since Floci keeps no automated backups, and answers\n`DBInstanceAutomatedBackupNotFound`. A restored instance takes the source's engine, version,\ncredentials, database name, storage and encryption, and its instance class unless the request names\none; everything else is the request's or the default a new instance gets. A restored cluster takes\nthe source's engine, version, credentials, database name and encryption, and has no instances until\nthey are added with `CreateDBInstance`, as on AWS.\n\nFloci keeps no transaction log, so it cannot rebuild a database as it was at an earlier time. The\ntarget is seeded from a `pg_dumpall` of the source taken when the request arrives, the mechanism read\nreplicas use, so the restored data is the source's latest state whatever time in the window is\nasked for; this is also why `LatestRestorableTime` is always the current time. As with\n`CreateDBSnapshot`, only PostgreSQL sources are accepted.\n\n## Global clusters\n\n`CreateGlobalCluster` creates an Aurora global database (`aurora-mysql` or `aurora-postgresql`),\neither empty or with an existing Aurora cluster as its primary through `SourceDBClusterIdentifier`\n(an ARN, or an identifier in the request's region), in which case engine, version, database name\nand encryption come from that cluster and may not be given, as on AWS. The record is account wide:\nits ARN has no region and `DescribeGlobalClusters` lists it from any region.\n\n`CreateDBCluster` with `GlobalClusterIdentifier` joins a cluster: the first one becomes the\nprimary, every later one a secondary. A secondary must be in a region that holds neither the\nprimary nor another secondary, may not carry its own master credentials or database name (it takes\nthe primary's), and its database is initialised from a `pg_dumpall` of the primary the way a read\nreplica is, so only `aurora-postgresql` primaries accept secondaries; writes after that are not\nstreamed. `DescribeGlobalClusters` reports every member with `IsWriter` and, on the primary, the\nsecondaries under `Readers`; `DescribeDBClusters` reports `GlobalClusterIdentifier` on members.\n\n`SwitchoverGlobalCluster`, and `FailoverGlobalCluster` with or without `AllowDataLoss`, promote\nthe named secondary and demote the current primary to a secondary, the topology AWS keeps for a\nswitchover and restores after a managed failover once the old primary region is healthy again.\nThe response is the completed state; AWS answers with a pending `FailoverState` because the\noperation runs asynchronously there. `RemoveFromGlobalCluster` detaches a member into a standalone\ncluster; the primary can only be removed once every secondary is gone, and deleting the primary\ncluster while secondaries remain is refused the same way. `DeleteGlobalCluster` needs an empty\nglobal cluster with deletion protection off.\n\n`FailoverDBCluster` moves the writer role inside a DB cluster to the named reader instance, or to\nthe first reader when none is named; a cluster with no reader has nothing to fail over to and is\nrefused. `DescribeDBClusters` reports the role as `IsClusterWriter`, and deleting the writer\npromotes a remaining member, as Aurora does on its own.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEach DB instance and cluster gets its own named Docker volume (`floci-rds-{volumeId}`) created\nautomatically. No configuration is required.\n\n| Scenario | Volume behavior |\n|---|---|\n| `memory` mode (default) | Volume is removed automatically when the instance is deleted |\n| `persistent` / `hybrid` / `wal` | Volume is retained after delete — data survives for manual recovery |\n\n```bash\n# CI — ephemeral, volumes cleaned up on each delete\nFLOCI_STORAGE_MODE=memory\n\n# Local dev — retain DB data across Floci restarts\nFLOCI_STORAGE_MODE=hybrid\n\n# Local dev — also remove volumes immediately on delete\nFLOCI_STORAGE_MODE=hybrid\nFLOCI_STORAGE_PRUNE_VOLUMES_ON_DELETE=true\n```\n\nTo use a host bind mount instead of a named volume (advanced), set an absolute path:\n\n```bash\nFLOCI_STORAGE_HOST_PERSISTENT_PATH=/absolute/host/path/data\n```\n\n!!! note \"Docker Desktop on macOS\"\n    Named volumes work correctly on Docker Desktop for macOS. Bind mounts to paths inside the Floci container are not supported — use named volumes (the default).\n\n## Authentication\n\nThe RDS auth proxy validates the master username and password at the proxy layer. All other database users are passed through directly to the backend engine — create them with standard SQL (`CREATE USER`) and connect as normal.\n\nIAM database authentication is also supported. Set `--enable-iam-database-authentication` at instance creation time and use `aws rds generate-db-auth-token` to obtain a token.\n\nA token can be signed with an access key or with temporary credentials: an assumed role's, or the execution role credentials Floci hands a Lambda function. A token signed with temporary credentials carries their session token in `X-Amz-Security-Token`, and it is accepted while that session is valid and only with the session token issued alongside the access key.\n\nOn RDS, a token is only good for the endpoint it was generated for: the hostname, port and region passed to `generate-db-auth-token` are the ones the instance (or cluster, or RDS Proxy) publishes. MySQL and MariaDB endpoints in Floci always refuse a token generated for another endpoint. PostgreSQL endpoints do the same by default; set `FLOCI_SERVICES_RDS_IAM_TOKEN_ENDPOINT_BINDING=false` to accept a token generated for another name, for clients that generate tokens for a container name or DNS alias the endpoint does not publish. Either way, the username must match the `DBUser` in the token exactly. Because clients on the host reach the same proxy over the loopback interface, a token generated for `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` on the published port is accepted as well. Clients on a Docker network connect by Floci's container name, so set `FLOCI_SERVICES_RDS_ENDPOINT_HOST` to that name (see [Docker Compose](#docker-compose)) so it is what the endpoint publishes and tokens are generated for. With [IAM enforcement](iam.md#iam-enforcement-mode) turned on, the token's principal must also be allowed `rds-db:connect` on the database user, scoped the way AWS scopes it:\n\n```\narn:aws:rds-db:<region>:<account-id>:dbuser:<DbiResourceId>/<db-user-name>\n```\n\nAurora clusters use the `DbClusterResourceId`, and connections through an RDS Proxy use the proxy's `prx-…` resource id. A token that fails any of these checks is refused with the engine's ordinary authentication failure; the reason is written to Floci's log.\n\nOn PostgreSQL, the token names a database role (`DBUser`) and the session runs as that role: `current_user` and `session_user` both report it, objects it creates are owned by it, and a token naming a role the database does not have is refused with `FATAL: role \"...\" does not exist`. Create the role first with `CREATE ROLE <name> WITH LOGIN` as the master user, and grant it whatever the application needs.\n\nUnderneath, the proxy reaches the container as the master user and hands the session over to the token's role, so an IAM session that talks its way back to the master role, via `RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION` and its variants, is terminated with `FATAL: permission denied to set session authorization` rather than being allowed to regain superuser. `SET ROLE` is untouched: PostgreSQL still permission-checks it against the token's role, exactly as on RDS. One difference from RDS: the proxy learns of the switch from PostgreSQL's own report, so when several statements are batched into a single query after the switch, their results are returned before the session is closed.\n\nThe parameters a PostgreSQL client sends when it connects (`options` such as `-c search_path=app`, `application_name`, and any other run-time parameter) apply to the session as they do on RDS. An IAM session for a role other than the master gets them once the session has been handed over to the token's role, applied with `set_config()` so PostgreSQL checks each one against that role's privileges, and a parameter PostgreSQL refuses fails the login with PostgreSQL's own error, as it would at startup. A `session_authorization` naming any other role is refused with `permission denied to set session authorization` before anything is applied, since PostgreSQL would authorize it against the master the proxy connected as. Because those sessions have already started, three things differ from RDS: `options` may carry only `-c name=value` and `--name=value` switches, a parameter that can only be set at connection start is refused with `cannot be set after connection start`, and `replication` connections are refused. And because the values are set with `set_config()` rather than at startup, `RESET` (and `RESET ALL`) takes such a parameter back to the server default, not to the value the client connected with: after `-c search_path=app`, `RESET search_path` gives `\"$user\", public` where RDS keeps `app`.\n\nOn MySQL, `AWSAuthenticationPlugin` is proprietary to RDS and ships in no public MySQL build, so\n`CREATE USER ... IDENTIFIED WITH AWSAuthenticationPlugin AS 'RDS'` would fail against the container\nwith `ERROR 1524 (HY000): Plugin 'AWSAuthenticationPlugin' is not loaded`. The proxy rewrites that\nclause to `IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password AS '*000...0'`, an authentication string no\npassword hashes to. The account is therefore created, can be granted to and can be dropped, but\nholds no password of its own, which is what an IAM DB user is: an account whose credentials come\nfrom IAM rather than from MySQL. This is the MySQL counterpart of the empty `rds_iam` role Floci\npre-creates for PostgreSQL.\n\nTwo limits follow from that. `SHOW CREATE USER` reports the substituted plugin rather than\n`AWSAuthenticationPlugin`, so a Terraform or Pulumi refresh sees drift on `auth_plugin`. And\nconnecting with a token is not yet emulated for MySQL: unlike PostgreSQL, which receives the\npassword in cleartext, MySQL sends a scramble, so the proxy would have to drive the\n`mysql_clear_password` auth switch that real RDS triggers before it could see a token to validate.\n\n## TLS / SSL\n\nThe RDS auth proxy terminates TLS itself (the backend container stays plaintext) using a\nself-signed CA whose Subject Alternative Names cover every advertised host Floci has handed\nout for a DB instance, cluster, or RDS Proxy — the Docker bridge IP, `host.docker.internal`,\n`localhost`, or whatever `rds.endpointHost` resolves to. The CA is persisted at\n`{storage.persistent-path}/tls/rds-ca.crt` and grows its SAN list as new hosts appear, so the\nsame root survives restarts and works for every local database, not just the one that\ngenerated it.\n\nFloci logs the certificate path (and the `PGSSLROOTCERT` hint) the first time it generates or\nloads it:\n\n```\nRDS proxy TLS: CA cert at ./data/tls/rds-ca.crt\nRDS proxy TLS: for sslmode=verify-full set PGSSLROOTCERT=./data/tls/rds-ca.crt\n```\n\nBecause the SAN matches the address you actually connect to, `verify-full` (the same level\nAurora enforces in AWS) works locally too — no need to fall back to `sslmode=disable` just to\nexercise the same connection-string settings you use in production:\n\n```bash\n# PostgreSQL\nPGSSLROOTCERT=./data/tls/rds-ca.crt psql \"host=localhost port=7001 user=admin sslmode=verify-full\"\n\n# MySQL / MariaDB\nmysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 7002 -u root -psecret123 \\\n  --ssl-mode=VERIFY_IDENTITY --ssl-ca=./data/tls/rds-ca.crt\n```\n","metadata":{"truncated":false},"title":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/floci-io/floci/main/docs/services/rds.md (text/plain; charset=utf-8)","time":{"start":1791622108166,"end":1791622108250}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_124ffd402001rGMYglemZhlLQ5","sessionID":"ses_edb00e85fffe6Tj3x1DWpDK53u","messageID":"msg_124ffc400001bUxj7VHkPQsGPJ"}}
